findings.statement: Gross margin was higher in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 than a year earlier: 75.0% against 72.4%, which the filing attributes to improved mix from Blackwell Ultra.
findings.rationale: The year-over-year increase is stated directly and has an operating cause (mix), not only a one-time effect. It is a comparison with the same quarter a year earlier, so it shows a rise over that period but not a continuing upward trend.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased to 75.0% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to 72.4% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, and 75.0% for the first half of fiscal year 2027 compared to 66.6% for the first half of fiscal year 2026 due to improved mix from Blackwell Ultra.

findings.statement: The first-quarter increase in fiscal 2027 (74.9% against 60.5%) is attributed primarily to the prior year's $4.5 billion H20 charge, so it mostly reflects the removal of a one-time item.
findings.rationale: The filing says the year-over-year rise was primarily due to the prior-year charge. That weakens the use of this comparison as evidence of underlying expansion.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased to 74.9% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to 60.5% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, primarily due to the prior year's $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

findings.statement: Gross margin was approximately flat sequentially in the most recent quarter. The reported quarterly figures are 75.0%, 74.9% and 75.0% for the last three quarters, which shows a plateau and not continued expansion.
findings.rationale: The company states that the sequential change was approximately flat. The three quarterly gross margin figures agree, so the claim of expansion holds only against year-ago periods that carried the charge and the transition costs.

quotes.text: Gross margin was approximately flat sequentially as our Blackwell architecture remains the vast majority of our revenue.

findings.statement: For the full fiscal year 2026, gross margin fell to 71.1% from 75.0% in fiscal 2025, so over the last full year it contracted.
findings.rationale: The annual figure fell, with the filing citing the shift from Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions and the H20 charge. The recent quarters recover to the fiscal 2025 level of 75.0% but do not exceed it.

quotes.text: Gross margins decreased to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions and a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026.

response.rationale: The passages show a recovery, not a steady expansion. Gross margin rose year over year in the first half of fiscal 2027, but part of that is the absence of the prior-year $4.5 billion H20 charge, and the company says it was approximately flat sequentially. The last full fiscal year saw a decline. The claim holds if it means a rebound from the depressed fiscal 2026 level and is not supported if it means margins are still rising.
unknowns: Whether gross margin will rise above the roughly 75% level in upcoming quarters; the passages give no forward guidance on gross margin.
